Task: List five surprising facts about the Roman Empire.

Here are five surprising facts about the Roman Empire:

1. Roman Concrete’s Secret Recipe  
   Unlike modern concrete, Roman seawall and harbor concrete actually became stronger over time. They mixed volcanic ash, lime (calcium oxide), and seawater, creating a chemical reaction that produced rare minerals reinforcing the structure—many of which still stand today.

2. Fast-Food Counters Called “Thermopolia”  
   In ancient Rome, many city dwellers without kitchens ate out. Thermopolia were small street-front shops serving hot foods and drinks. Archaeologists have even found counters with built-in dolia (jars) for holding hot soups and stews—an early form of fast food.

3. Emperor Caligula’s “Consul” Horse  
   Caligula, known for eccentricity (and cruelty), is said to have planned making his favorite horse, Incitatus, a consul. He reportedly lavished the animal with a marble stall, an ivory manger, and a jeweled collar to mock the senatorial elite.

4. Purple Dye Worth Its Weight in Gold  
   The famous Tyrian purple dye came from murex sea snails. Extracting just a small quantity required tens of thousands of snails and a laborious process. As a result, purple garments were extraordinarily expensive and reserved for emperors and high-ranking officials.

5. Urine as a Cleaning Agent and Mouthwash  
   Ancient Romans collected urine for its ammonia content and used it in laundries to whiten togas. It was also mixed with water as a sort of mouthwash. Public urinals even had collecting jars so fullers (laundry workers) could harvest the liquid.
